subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this cold-start hang by making Docker sandbox control-plane deadlines and fail-soft sandbox unavailability the default behavior, or require more macOS/OrbStack diagnostics before changing the default runtime contract?
rationale: The source-level no-timeout path is clear, but the reported intermittent stall is broader than Docker exec alone and the likely fix changes compatibility-sensitive sandbox startup behavior.

options.title: Refresh the timeout/fail-soft fix
options.body: Review or replace the linked PR so it bounds the full Docker prune/init/hash path, preserves current sandbox workspace behavior, documents the default, and includes real wedged-Docker or OrbStack proof.

options.title: Collect diagnostics first
options.body: Keep the issue in maintainer review and ask for trace logs or a live reproduction that isolates whether prune, skill sync, Docker user resolution, or Docker control-plane calls dominate the stall.

options.title: Narrow to the canonical Docker bug
options.body: Treat this issue as a partial overlap with the narrower wedged-Docker issue and only close it after that fix lands if no distinct workspace-prep evidence remains.

recommendation.title: Refresh the timeout/fail-soft fix
recommendation.body: Review or replace the linked PR so it bounds the full Docker prune/init/hash path, preserves current sandbox workspace behavior, documents the default, and includes real wedged-Docker or OrbStack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: History ties this person to sandbox prune, registry, cleanup, and config/security boundaries, which are the main product/default decisions left open.
